clue.text: Fantastically great concert, absurd performance

parts.note: a gig is a live music concert
an antic is a piece of absurd or grotesque behaviour

explanation.surface: A reviewer raves about a wonderful concert while mocking a ridiculous turn on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Something enormous is fantastically great in size, a synonym for huge.

clue.text: Hog ultimately shrill as a pig!

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Hog

parts.note: a reedy voice is thin and shrill

explanation.surface: A squealing hog sounds as high-pitched as any pig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hog' looks like the definition but only gives its last letter; the definition is 'as a pig', describing a gluttonous animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigs are proverbially gluttonous, so behaving as a pig means being insatiable at the trough.

clue.text: Frightful noise of bear

indicators.note: noise of says we want how a word sounds when spoken

parts.note: a grizzly is a large North American bear

explanation.surface: A camper describes the terrifying growl of a bear in the night.
explanation.definitionFit: Gruesome and horrifying things are frightful, the same sense of causing dread.

clue.text: Title including religious text, coloured in church

indicators.note: including means the title word holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a title is a name
OT is the Old Testament
red is a colour, so coloured can give red, as in flushed

explanation.surface: A heading in a church notice picks out a scriptural passage in colour.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous Paris cathedral, named for Our Lady, is a church.

clue.text: Horrid news to broadcast? I mean to say!

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone flinches at terrible news being aired and gropes for a gentler phrasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases introduce a rephrasing of what was just said, an idiom of clarification.

clue.text: This thick-skinned? We need to hear from you!

definitions.meaning: a patch of hardened, thickened skin, such as on a hand or foot

definitions.text: We need to hear from you
definitions.meaning: read as two words, a plea to telephone us, the line of a radio phone-in

explanation.surface: A broadcaster asks listeners to phone in, as if soliciting views from someone hard to offend.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardened skin forms a thick pad, which is what the first definition describes.

clue.text: Duck breaking wing, requiring a scent

indicators.note: breaking means one piece splits the other open and sits within it

parts.note: an arm is a wing of a building or organisation
a duck in cricket is a score of nought, the letter O

explanation.surface: A wounded duck with a broken wing needs a trail of scent to be found.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasant smell or fragrance is a scent, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Bacon not quite admitting age, as old artist

indicators.note: admitting means letting the age piece inside
not quite means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: a lardon is a small strip of bacon
an eon is an age

explanation.surface: Francis Bacon, the painter, nearly admitting his age as an old master.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bacon' suggests the painter, but is just a cooking strip; 'not quite' leaves LARDO.
explanation.definitionFit: Da Vinci, the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa, is an old artist.

clue.text: Very modern patrol in a shade of green

indicators.note: in places the patrol word inside the colour word

parts.note: sage is a greyish shade of green
to pace is to walk up and down, as a sentry on patrol

explanation.surface: A futuristic police patrol is kitted out in a fashionable green.
explanation.definitionFit: The era of rockets and satellites gives an adjective for something ultra-modern.

clue.text: Unfortunate notice, six being housed — this getting them out?

indicators.note: being housed means the number sits inside the rearranged letters
unfortunate suggests things gone wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Tenants receive a grim notice, six of them living there, warning they will be thrown out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unfortunate' jumbles the notice into ECTION, and 'being housed' puts the Roman six within; the definition is the whole closing phrase, the process itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Expelling tenants from a property is the process that gets them out.

clue.text: Kick around Guyanese capital, a South American city

indicators.note: around means the kick word surrounds the letter

parts.note: to boot is to kick

indicators.note: capital here means the first, or capital, letter of the word

explanation.surface: Footballers boot the ball around Georgetown, Guyana's capital, then a rival South American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guyanese capital' tempts one to think of Georgetown; it is only the initial G.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of Colombia is a major city of that continent.

clue.text: Pompous type has beaten Garibaldi, say?

parts.note: stuffed is slang for soundly beaten or defeated
a garibaldi is a loose blouse or shirt, after the red shirts of Garibaldi's followers

explanation.surface: A self-important figure claims to have defeated the Italian patriot Garibaldi.
explanation.walkthrough: Garibaldi suggests the general (or a biscuit), but here it is a style of shirt.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for a pompous, stuffy and self-satisfied person.

clue.text: Berk repulsed, revenge finally sweet

indicators.note: repulsed means driven back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: berk is British slang for a fool, a clod

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word revenge

explanation.surface: An idiot is beaten back and revenge, at last, tastes sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian musical direction means sweetly, also used for dessert wines and sweets.

clue.text: The charts moved apart, leather-bound?

indicators.note: bound means wrapped round, so the leather word encloses the other letters

parts.note: hide is animal skin, leather

indicators.note: moved means the letters are shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: A leather-bound record of the charts falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leather-bound' looks like one adjective but splits: 'leather' is the skin and 'bound' wraps it round the letters that 'moved' shuffles.
explanation.definitionFit: The list of best-selling records is the music charts, a synonym from pop radio.

clue.text: Getting drunk, I forgot head hurts at first -—- try this?

indicators.note: at first points to the initial letter of the word hurts
getting drunk means becoming muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drinker who forgot their aching head is offered a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is I FORGOT HEAD plus H, the first letter of 'hurts'.
explanation.definitionFit: Another drink to cure a hangover is the traditional remedy suggested to the sufferer.

clue.text: The item: a doubly poor source of iron

indicators.note: poor means badly made, so the letters are rearranged
doubly means the single letter a is used twice over

explanation.surface: A shoddy item is a doubly poor source of iron.
explanation.definitionFit: This reddish mineral is iron oxide, the main ore mined for iron.

clue.text: Description of superwaif wearing shoe in wardrobe

indicators.note: wearing means one word has the other inside it, as a foot sits in a shoe

parts.note: a clog is a wooden shoe
a superwaif is a very skinny model, described as slender

explanation.surface: A skinny model's clog is described as she dresses from her wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: One's wardrobe is the collection of garments one owns.

clue.text: Place under surveillance first of suspects, then kill

indicators.note: first of points to the opening letter of the word suspects

parts.note: to take out is slang for to kill

explanation.surface: Police watch suspects before an assassination.
explanation.definitionFit: A police watch on a place is a noun, but here the verb sense to watch secretly fits.

clue.text: Dear as a knife may be?

definitions.meaning: the word that begins a note to someone, as in Dear Sir
a blunt blade for slitting envelopes

explanation.surface: A shopper finds a knife expensive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dear' looks like expensive, but it is the first word of correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: The salutation is the opening of correspondence, and the knife slits envelopes.

clue.text: Man of musicals, passable composer

parts.note: Lionel Bart wrote the stage musical Oliver!
OK means passable, acceptable

explanation.surface: A musicals writer is judged a passable composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla, the Hungarian, wrote orchestral and piano works and is a composer.

clue.text: Tree's canopy a mistake for monkey

indicators.note: a canopy is the top of a tree, so the first letter of the word Tree's

parts.note: an error is a mistake

explanation.surface: A monkey in the treetops is taken for something it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'monkey' suggests the animal, but means a naughty child.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child is called a little monkey, or a little terror.

clue.text: King in the main backed amid ups and downs; choose who to support

indicators.note: amid means the reversed piece sits inside the other

parts.note: tides rise and fall

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, read from the end
in places the king letter inside the sea word

parts.note: the main is a poetic term for the sea
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A king, amid the turbulent sea, must decide whom to back.
explanation.walkthrough: SEKA, backed, gives AKES inside TIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick a party to support in an argument is an idiom for taking a position.

clue.text: Line cutting margin, inch

indicators.note: cutting means the letter slices into the other word

parts.note: a side is an edge, margin

explanation.surface: A line across the page margin measures an inch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inch' looks like a unit of measure, but is the verb to creep sideways.
explanation.definitionFit: To edge furtively along is to move slowly and cautiously, like inching forward.

clue.text: Bodies in the ground alongside a stone

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports ground

explanation.surface: Bodies are buried in a graveyard beside a headstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' suggests burial, but is a football ground and its crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A banded form of chalcedony is a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Operatic heroine has a bus pass that's heading for expiry

parts.note: in Britain pensioners get a free bus pass, so the holder is aged, read as is old

indicators.note: heading for points to the first letter of the word expiry

explanation.surface: A singer's bus pass is about to expire.
explanation.definitionFit: Wagner's tragic lover in Tristan und Isolde is the opera heroine.

clue.text: Left at home, nurse tending?

indicators.note: tending means caring around, so the nurse word encloses the home word

parts.note: a sister is a senior nurse
in means at home

explanation.surface: Left at home with a nurse caring for the patient.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for left-hand gives the heraldic term for the left side.

clue.text: Good total viewing dirty channel?

parts.note: utter means complete, total

explanation.surface: Good grief, viewing an absolutely filthy television channel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'channel' suggests television; it is a drain.
explanation.definitionFit: The roadside drain carrying filthy water is a dirty channel.

clue.text: Person running out of habits

parts.note: habits suggests nuns' garb or routines, but here means clothes; a naked runner dashes out of them

explanation.surface: Someone breaking free of habits, or a nun fleeing her habit.
explanation.definitionFit: A nude runner at a sports event has run out of their clothes.
